title: Flatten nested JSON order events with PySpark
objective_text: Parse a JSON text column with from_json and a schema, turn each order's array of line items into one row per line with explode_outer, and write a typed Silver table without the raw JSON.
scenario: The shop's order API lands one JSON document per order in bronze.order_events: the order's id, customer and time, and an items array with each line's sku, quantity and price. Finance wants silver.order_lines with one typed row per order line. Some orders arrive with an empty items list, or with none at all, and Finance wants to see those too, so such an order keeps one row in silver.order_lines with sku, qty and price empty (NULL), never zero rows.
engine_label: DuckDB's PySpark API on this PC (not Apache Spark)
starting_environment: The Delta table bronze.order_events (event_id, and payload: the JSON text) in the exercise folder, and a starter answer.py.
required: One row per line item, and one row for an order whose items list is empty or missing, with sku, qty and price NULL.
order_id and qty are integers, placed_at is a timestamp, price is a decimal and customer_id and sku are text.
Every row has its order's order_id, customer_id and placed_at.
Write silver.order_lines with order_id, customer_id, placed_at, sku, qty, price and no other column, so that running the code again leaves the same table.

expected.description: silver.order_lines has 8 rows: two for order 101, three for 104, one for 105, and one each for 102 and 103 with no sku.

verifies: Your PySpark parses the JSON, flattens the line items and keeps orders without lines, on the exercise data and on orders you haven't seen with their keys in another order and extra fields, on this PC.
silver.order_lines has exactly the columns asked for, with the types asked for, no empty order key, and one row per order and sku.
Running it again leaves the same table.
does_not_verify: It doesn't run on Apache Spark or in a Fabric notebook. Here from_json is called through F.expr with the schema written as text, because F.from_json with a StructType isn't available on this PC. In a Fabric notebook both forms work.
Malformed JSON: every document here parses. It doesn't show the corrupt-record column or the FAILFAST mode.
Inferring the schema from the files with spark.read.json, and how Spark plans the explode on large tables.
That the table is a lakehouse table in OneLake: here it's a Delta table in the exercise folder on this PC.
The SQL and KQL parts of the objective, which other exercises cover.

validation.pass: silver.order_lines holds the right rows for the practice data.
validation.fail: silver.order_lines doesn't match: check the orders without lines, the field names in your schema and the columns you keep.

validation.pass: It also works on orders you haven't seen.
validation.fail: It doesn't hold on other orders: don't rely on the order of the keys in the JSON or on these exact documents.

hints: Read the JSON with a schema: F.expr("from_json(payload, 'order_id INT, customer_id STRING, ...')"). An array of structs is written ARRAY<STRUCT<name: TYPE, ...>>.
A field the schema names differently from the JSON key comes back NULL for every row, with no error, so the names must match the keys exactly.
F.explode drops a row whose array is empty or NULL, and F.explode_outer keeps it, with a NULL element.
Reach into a struct with F.col("o.order_id") or F.col("item.sku"), and alias each column to its final name.
get_json_object always returns text: if you use it, cast every value it gives.
explanation: from_json reads the JSON text once, by a schema you write, so every field arrives with its type: order_id an integer, placed_at a timestamp, price a decimal. A field is matched by its key, not by position, so documents with their keys in another order or with extra fields parse the same; a schema field whose name doesn't match any key quietly comes back NULL. explode turns an array into one row per element and copies the order's other columns onto each, but it gives no row at all for an empty or NULL array, so orders without lines would disappear. explode_outer keeps them as one row with a NULL element. get_json_object is fine for a single value, but it returns text, so its results need casting. Select only the typed columns, so the raw JSON doesn't travel into Silver, and overwrite so a rerun gives the same table.
troubleshooting: Orders 102 and 103 are missing: explode drops an empty or missing array, so use explode_outer.
customer_id (or another field) is NULL on every row: its name in the schema doesn't match the JSON key.
order_id or placed_at is VARCHAR: it came from get_json_object, which returns text, so read it with from_json or cast it.
The column check names payload: select only the six columns, without the raw JSON.
reset: Reset rebuilds bronze.order_events from setup.sql, removes silver.order_lines and puts the starter back.
review_notes: F.from_json isn't in DuckDB's PySpark API or spark_compat's FUNCTIONS, so the brief, starter and hints use F.expr("from_json(payload, '<DDL schema>')"), which goes through the Spark SQL translation checked against Spark 3.5 (spark_json.py, WR-118). That form is valid PySpark in Fabric too.
Spark's JSON reader matches a schema field to its key exactly, so wrong-schema-field-name (customerId for customer_id) gives NULL there as it does here.
unique on order_id and sku holds because no order in either data set lists a sku twice; an order without lines has one row with a NULL sku.
